title: NILS pack manifest
description: The pack.yml of a modality pack: what the pack is, and which files hold its parsers, flags, axes, rules, passes, picks, private lists, dictionary and BIDS mapping. Every file list is relative to the pack directory. Version 2 adds the optional fields key. Version 3 adds the optional levels key. Version 4 adds the optional mcp key. Version 5 adds no key: it opens every axis value's keywords list to an overlay, named lists.<axis>.<value> beside the buckets, and writes the overlay document down as overlay.schema.json beside this one. The flags, the physics windows, the review thresholds and the order values are tried in stay the pack's. Version 6 (record 48) adds two optional keys, excludes and hints: files of constraints between axes, over axis values alone. An exclusion rules values of one axis out when its condition holds (hard: an answer holding both is refused); a hint names the value usually found on an axis when its condition holds, with its reason (soft: shown, never enforced). Neither decides an axis of a stack. An engine at 6 loads a contract-5 pack unchanged. Version 7 (record 51) adds no manifest key: the picks files it names gain v0's six other border reasons (retake, unknown_dim, slice_outlier, pre_post_twin, fallback, dixon_vs_plain) and a list of families, each with a name, what a family without its canonical output becomes (without_canonical) and when it is a retake (retake_above). A role a pick scores with tables per role must have its own in every such component. An engine at 7 loads a contract-6 pack unchanged, and refuses those keys in a pack that declares less than 7, so an engine at 6 refuses the pack rather than picking without them. Version 8 (record 53) adds no manifest key: a passes file may declare a pass of kind session_context, whose target and rules read what a rule reads and whose rules alone may read the other stacks of a stack's session, each sibling seen by its header through the fields the pass names (session.sibling_fields), never by what was decided of it; it never replaces a value a header tier (a flag or a number the scanner wrote), a person or a decision set, and one read from the name, inferred, defaulted or voted only at or below session.replaces_at_most, and writes tier session. A picks file's fallback border may name a list of values (is). A private file may list the ingested elements a reader is shown (shown: name and why), each an ingested element of a technical kind at an address the engine may show, and shown at every detail; the quasi: true an entry could carry in 1.0.0-alpha.66 and .67, which held a vendor's sequence name back below detail quasi, is withdrawn (1.0.0-alpha.68: sequence names are shown at every detail), and an engine ignores it. An engine at 8 loads a contract-7 pack unchanged, and refuses those keys in a pack that declares less than 8, so an engine at 7 refuses the pack rather than reading it without them. Version 9 (the 2026-10-10 study of the pick borders) adds no manifest key: a picks file may say which stacks holding a role compete for it (candidates, per role, when and unless lists of conditions, each {of, any: [values]} or {of, lt | le | gt | ge: number} over a name the pick reads; a stack that is no candidate for a role is no part of its population either) and how a near tie is decided (near_tie, a list of steps, each {of, prefer: [values]}, {of, avoid: [values]}, {of, lowest: true} or {of, highest: true}, for every role or the roles it names: among the candidates within runner_up_within of the best, the first step that tells the first two apart decides, and a near tie it decides is no border). An engine at 9 loads a contract-8 pack unchanged, and refuses those keys in a pack that declares less than 9, so an engine at 8 refuses the pack rather than picking without them.

pack.description: The pack's name, which is also its directory's name.

contract.description: The pack contract this manifest was written for. An engine implementing a lower one refuses the pack.

modality.description: The DICOM modality the pack judges (MR, CT, PT).

parsers.description: Parser files: a parser tokenises a text field and names predicates over its tokens.

flags.description: Flag files: named boolean expressions over the fingerprint, the parsers and other flags.

normalize.description: Normalizer files: the text the pack derives for itself from the fingerprint's fields, published as fields of the pack.

axes.description: Axis files, in the order the axes are decided; an axis may read one declared before it.

rules.description: Rule sets written longhand, after the axes they decide.

excludes.description: Files of exclusions between axes (record 48), each `excludes:` a list of {id, when, excludes: {axis, is | any | family}, why, sources}: when the condition over axis values holds, the named values of the other axis are ruled out, and an answer holding one is refused. Frozen into a campaign with the implications.

hints.description: Files of hints (record 48), each `hints:` a list of {id, when, suggest: {axis, value}, why, sources, counter?}: the value usually found on an axis when the condition over axis values holds, with its reason. Shown to a reader, never enforced, never a certificate's.

order.description: The order the rule sets run in, by name; a set not named here never runs and is refused.

passes.description: Pass files: the phases that read more than one stack.

picks.description: Pick files: which stack stands for a session's role.

private.description: Private element files: the ingest list the digest reads, the release list a release keeps, and the vendor coverage.

dictionary.description: Private dictionary files, tab-separated: creator, group, offset, VR, VM, name.

bids.description: BIDS mapping files: which of the pack's values means which BIDS suffix, datatype and entity.

review.description: When a person is asked about an axis.

low_confidence.description: The confidence below which an axis is asked about: one number for every axis, or a map with a default and per-axis overrides.

missing.description: The axes whose absence is itself a question.

by_model.description: The axes an operation of their own answers, an image model in its own run with its own review of what it is unsure of: sorting raises no question about them at all, and what the rules state of them is kept as they state it (added in place on 2026-10-10; the MRI pack names body_part, body_region and post_contrast).

silent_when.description: A condition under which nobody is asked about a stack at all.

buckets.description: The named lists a site may amend through an overlay by name, beside every axis value's keywords list, which an overlay amends as lists.<axis>.<value> (version 5). Nothing else of the pack is a site's to amend.

fields.description: Wave 4a section 11.2 (C27): the visibility the pack puts on a catalogue field, by field name. local is this node only (free text, paths, exact dates, identifiers); federated is on the allowlist a peer may read; sensitive is never released and never read by a peer. Read by nothing in this wave; the catalog of the question wave and the federation of Wave 8 read it.

levels.description: Comparability level files (Wave 4b section 6): what the same acquisition means at each named level. Every axis and the acquisition type compare exactly at every level; the numeric physics compare rounded to a declared step, or not at all.

mcp.description: What the MCP door tells a model (Wave 4b section 12.3): which doors are opted in as tools, what each says about itself, the grounding rules every listing carries, and the few-shot documents. One file; it ships in the pack so a model behaviour change does not cut an engine release.
